# Dayglass for macOS

> Your private AI memory for work: bot-free meeting notes for Mac, readable live by Claude Code and Cursor over MCP, with Apple Vision Neural Engine OCR, ScreenCaptureKit bot-free headphone/AirPods call recording, 384K SubQ Snap 3-Way Hybrid GraphRAG, On-Device AI Companion 3.0 with OpenUI Generative UI cards, and Vitalik 4-layer Paranoid Mode.

## Canonical Install & Download Links
- Homepage & Interactive Demo: https://igorganapolsky.github.io/dayglass-mac/
- 1-Line Terminal Installer: `curl -fsSL https://igorganapolsky.github.io/dayglass-mac/install.sh | bash`
- Homebrew Cask: `brew install --cask igorganapolsky/dayglass/dayglass`
- Direct Apple-Notarized DMG (latest release): https://github.com/IgorGanapolsky/dayglass-mac/releases/latest/download/Dayglass.dmg
- SHA-256: listed in SHA256SUMS on the latest release page

## Why Developers & Executives Choose Dayglass Over Cloud Bots (Fathom, Otter, Screenpipe, MacPaw Eney)
- Bot-Free AirPods & Headphone Call Recording: Uses native macOS `ScreenCaptureKit` (~93 MB RAM vs 4.58 GB Electron bloat). No virtual audio driver (BlackHole) and no cloud bot joining Zoom, Microsoft Teams, or Google Meet calls.
- Privacy: audio, screen and the database stay on your Mac in `~/.dayglass`. If you turn on a cloud model for Ask AI, the question and the relevant meeting text go to that model after emails, phone numbers, secrets and known names are swapped for placeholders. With a local model nothing leaves the Mac.
- 384,000-Token SubQ Snap Hybrid GraphRAG: Combines BM25 keyword search, 256-dim dense semantic vectors, and a 2-hop entity graph for cross-meeting recall in ~75ms.
- Built-In MCP Server for Coding Agents: Connects directly to Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, Poolside, and Oh-My-Pi (`python3 -m dayglass mcp`).
- Live meeting for other agents: while a Zoom, Teams, or Google Meet call is in progress, Claude, Cursor, and the other agents on the same Mac read the speaker-tagged transcript, the people on the call, and the shared screen through the local tool `dayglass_get_live_meeting`. The audio stays in `~/.dayglass`.
